scope: Reconciliation of the six existing grouped records and shared convention summaries; representative coverage only

notations.geometry: Rounded rectangular usage node; the illustrated composite and reference forms share the same basic geometry.
notations.line_style: Solid outline for the composite example; dashed outline for the reference example.
notations.labels: Part usage prefix and name/type follow part-name-compartment and usage-name-with-alias; the example uses «part» and «ref part».
notations.compartments: The grammar permits an interconnection view and compartment stack. These are not fully illustrated.
notations.attachments: port-t, port-b, port-l and port-r positions are permitted by the part production; side ports are not illustrated here.
notations.applicability: A referential part remains a PartUsage. The redraw demonstrates outline and label forms, not every permitted part context.
notations.alternatives: Composite and referential forms are grouped here. Compartment contents, boundary attachments and prefix combinations need further audit.
notations.illustrated_forms: One solid composite part node and one dashed referential part node.

notations.line_style: Solid outline in the original redraw.
notations.labels: Definition prefix, part def keyword and definition-name-with-alias; the minimal example uses «part def».
notations.compartments: Interconnection contents and a compartment stack may extend the definition node; omitted in the minimal redraw.
notations.attachments: The part-def production provides top, bottom, left and right port positions; these remain unillustrated.
notations.applicability: Represents a part definition rather than a particular usage of that definition.
notations.alternatives: Boundary ports, additional prefixes, aliases and compartment contents remain to be audited separately.
notations.illustrated_forms: Minimal part definition node with keyword and name.

notations.geometry: Full rounded usage node or small rounded boundary glyph. The boundary redraw illustrates one attachment position.
notations.line_style: Solid full node. The old compact outline omits direction geometry and is only an outline primitive; displayed boundary alternatives include pdh/pdv indicators.
notations.labels: The full form uses the port-name-compartment. Boundary labels use QualifiedName with an optional colon and QualifiedName.
notations.compartments: Full nodes can have a compartment stack and nested ports. Neither is exhausted by the illustration.
notations.attachments: The grammar gives separate left, right, top and bottom boundary productions with position-specific labels.
notations.applicability: Use boundary position and optional direction indications according to the corresponding port production; one drawn position does not cover all four.
notations.alternatives: All four orientations, direction glyphs, nesting and proxy alternatives require distinct checks. No direction is inferred from the undirected glyph.
notations.illustrated_forms: Full port usage node and compact outline primitive; new direction glyphs and a four-side composition are separately listed in the SVG library.

notations.geometry: Reference port outlines and proxy-dot alternatives are described from the source; there is no local redraw.
notations.line_style: The source note restricts dotted-line port productions to nested ports; no general rule for all ports is asserted.
notations.labels: Reference forms reuse port-label. Proxy forms reuse proxy-label, resolved in §8.2.3.9 (PDF 239) as an optional leading dot followed by FeatureChainMember.
notations.compartments: The nested-port context is part of the applicability restriction, not evidence that arbitrary diagram nesting implies ownership.
notations.attachments: Horizontal and vertical proxy productions correspond to side attachment alternatives.
notations.applicability: Dotted reference ports are possible only for nested ports. A proxy option is valid only on a part usage contained within an interconnection view.
notations.alternatives: Reference, elongated nested and proxy layouts remain deferred. The selected audit retains the port/port-usage spelling mismatch and keeps these cases separate.
notations.represents: SysML PortUsage and restricted proxy connection points

notations.geometry: Rounded full connection usage node or binary line joining connection ends.
notations.line_style: Solid line for the binary example; optional direction-indication arrow is not drawn and does not by itself assert flow semantics.
notations.labels: The node uses connection-name-compartment; the edge has an optional connection-label. Role names, multiplicities and c-adornment are separate grammar elements.
notations.compartments: The full connection node can contain a compartment stack, omitted in the minimal redraw.
notations.attachments: The binary grammar uses connection-end, which can be a usage-node or usage-edge.
notations.applicability: The redraw covers a connection usage node and undirected binary representation; it is not the definition-edge or binding notation.
notations.alternatives: Directed indication, adornments, end labels, elaboration and proxy connections remain unillustrated.
notations.illustrated_forms: Undirected binary connection line and minimal full connection usage node.

notations.geometry: Filled central dot with segments to usage nodes, as described in the graphical grammar.
notations.line_style: Solid segments; source description only, without a local redraw.
notations.labels: Central cdot-label uses UsageDeclaration; each segment has role name and multiplicity elements.
notations.compartments: This record describes the n-ary relationship form rather than a full node compartment stack.
notations.attachments: Each n-ary-segment links the central n-ary-connection-dot to a usage-node.
notations.applicability: Representative n-ary usage connection; do not substitute the separate n-ary definition grammar or infer arbitrary endpoint semantics.
notations.alternatives: The definition dot/segments are separate productions. End labels and all cardinality/context rules need a full audit.

shared_rules.title: Views contain nodes, edges and connection points
shared_rules.description: Graphical views render nodes connected by edges. Definition and usage nodes may have ports or parameter connection points. These are presentation structures, not automatically model ownership.

shared_rules.title: Compartments and selection
shared_rules.description: A node may have compartments. Each compartment is a view of selected members, rendered textually or graphically as specified by its grammar. Record selection and rendering separately.

shared_rules.title: Complete and partial productions
shared_rules.description: Table 30 distinguishes complete productions from distributed partial productions. Repeated production names retain every source occurrence; the register flags reversed or spaced operators without silently repairing the source.

shared_rules.title: Layout and stretching
shared_rules.description: The graphical grammar generally constrains containment and connectivity. Elements may generally be relocated and stretched to fit their contents. A redraw layout is not a unique required coordinate system.

shared_rules.title: Connecting lines and jumps
shared_rules.description: Connecting lines may have straight or curved segments. Segments may have a semicircular jump where they overlap another connecting line.

shared_rules.title: Imported textual productions
shared_rules.description: Graphical grammar symbols conventionally use lowercase names and hyphens. Mixed-case references import textual productions from §8.2.2; their dependencies must be reviewed rather than treated as new visual symbols.

shared_rules.title: Selecting an element inside a textual compartment
shared_rules.description: The source specifies graying a substring covering one element in a textual compartment. Selection highlighting is distinct from the permanent appearance of that element.

shared_rules.title: Names and aliases
shared_rules.description: Definition and usage name productions reuse textual declarations and can append alias labels. The usage-name-with-alias production also has an optional caret. Prefix and inherited/derived marker semantics require their textual and Clause 7 evidence.

shared_rules.title: Metadata keyword extensions
shared_rules.description: The extended definition/usage productions have applicability notes requiring an extension keyword to name a MetadataDefinition directly or indirectly specializing the KerML SemanticMetadata metaclass. A full KerML dependency audit remains open.

shared_rules.title: Standard views and valid contents
shared_rules.description: Table 34 names eight standard view definitions and associates five with default-compartment grammar sections; geometry, grid and browser entries have blank default-compartment cells. View content/filter requirements are a separate dependency audit. The §8.2.3.26 note references §9.2.18 while the actual package is §9.2.20.
